annotations.title: The Hebrew or Greek words of a verse

description: Return the original Hebrew or Greek words of a verse from stored data, never from memory: each Hebrew word (Westminster Leningrad Codex) or Greek word (Robinson-Pierpont Byzantine text) with its Strong's number, lexical form and transliteration, the definition and King James usage from Strong's public domain dictionary, the parsing in plain words (Open Scriptures Hebrew morphology, CC BY; Byzantine parsing codes, public domain), and the King James words that render it where the KJV-Strong's tagging links them. Use for word study ("what Greek word is love in John 21:15-17", "what does bara mean in Genesis 1:1", "is it agape or phileo"). Not for the verse in English or another language (scripture_passage, compare_translations) or for a topic (what_the_bible_says_about). reference is one verse (a range reads at most three); strong filters to one Strong's number such as "G25" or "H1254". Definitions and parsing are scholarship about the words, labelled as interpretation in content_layers, not Scripture. Books outside the Hebrew and Greek canon (the deuterocanon) return an error, as does a verse not in the stored text or a strong number absent from the verse. Deterministic, no network. Access: no sign-in; shared limit of 300 requests a minute per IP.

reference.description: One verse, e.g. "John 3:16" or "Genesis 1:1"; a range reads up to three verses.

strong.description: Optional: only the words with this Strong's number, e.g. "G25" or "H1254".

name: original_words

attribution.description: Credit line for the data: The Living Bread (living-bread.org).

content_layers.description: Which fields are Scripture and which are human interpretation or reflection.

door.description: Web page for Bible word study.

evidence.description: Present when Scripture was read: translation, canon, corpus version, attribution, and a SHA-256 per passage.

freshness.description: How current the answer is: kind (scheduled | recently_observed | verified_live | record), retrieved_at, available_now (true only when activity was verified live).

ids.description: Up to 25 ids found in this answer, for follow-up calls.

kjv_alignment.description: The source of the KJV word to Strong's links.

lexicon.description: The dictionary the definitions come from.

license.description: License URL of the returned data (CC BY 4.0 unless stated).

next_actions.description: Up to 4 links the person can open next.

ok.description: Always true on a successful answer (errors come back as isError, never here).

ref.description: The verse or verses read, in KJV numbering.

result_state.description: "empty" when nothing matched (count 0, no results); the text then says so plainly.

source_url.description: The first public web page this answer came from or points to.

text_source.description: The stored original-language text the words come from.

verses.description: Each verse: ref, own_ref when the numbering differs, the original text, and words in order with position, word, strong, translit, lemma and lemma_translit, pronunciation, part_of_speech, definition, kjv_usage, derivation, morph and morph_readable, and kjv_words.

visibility.description: "public" for shared data, "yours" for the signed-in believer's own data.

title: The Hebrew or Greek words of a verse
